name: Humeral Avulsion of Glenohumeral Ligament / HAGL Lesion
tags: humeral avulsion of glenohumeral ligament / hagl lesion
definition: Avulsion of the inferior glenohumeral ligament from its humeral attachment, an important cause of persistent shoulder instability.

investigations.principle: MRI or MR arthrography is used to identify humeral-sided capsuloligamentous avulsion.
investigations.MRI: Use MRI when neural, soft-tissue, labral, tendon, cartilage, ligament or occult injury assessment requires it.
investigations.radiographs: Use radiographs and/or CT according to the condition-specific diagnostic pathway.

amber: Persistent symptomatic HAGL lesions commonly require surgical repair.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Amsa-Snayu instability phenotype may be documented.

patientEducation.summary: Avulsion of the inferior glenohumeral ligament from its humeral attachment, an important cause of persistent shoulder instability.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute neurovascular compromise, unreduced dislocation, major trauma, rapidly progressive weakness, suspected tendon rupture, infection or other listed red flags.
